_description: Master card deck: every grapheme with all its pronunciations (front/back card model) plus every extra spelling. Each entry carries the level it may first appear from, so the natural progression is protected. Powers the in-book Shifty Sounds section, the games and the decodability engine.
_rule: A grapheme+sound pair is only decodable in a book at or above its allowed_from level. Below that level a word using it is tricky-for-now (pre-taught via its game).

_decisions.band_colour: LOCKED 2026-07-03 by Lynden: #475569 charcoal/slate grey. Deliberately outside the 8-level rainbow (see graphemes_by_level.json level colours) so it never reads as a 9th level.
_decisions.main_ladder_promotions: LOCKED 2026-07-03 by Lynden: confirmed all 8 as specialist-recommended, no additions. These 8 GPCs should be moved OUT of this Shifty Sounds data (or flagged non-shifty) and INTO data/graphemes_by_level.json at their natural level during the build: wh, ph, ve, -ed (3 sounds: /d/ /t/ /id/), y=/ee/, y=/igh/, soft c, soft g. The borderline extras (tch, dge, short oo, s=/z/, ea=/e/, au) STAY in the Shifty band, not promoted. IMPLEMENTED 2026-07-12: wh/ve/ph added to graphemes_by_level.json (levels 4/5/6); ed left as a suffix (already structurally present via level_7 suffixes, full suffix-aware decoding still pending); y=/igh/, y=/ee/, soft c, soft g pronunciation entries removed from this file (no longer shown as Shifty -- they need dedicated per-book Watch Out notes, not yet written). CORRECTION 2026-07-12: the ve promotion was attempted as a blanket grapheme in graphemes_by_level.json but reverted the same day -- it collided with ordinary magic-e words that happen to end in v (wave, five, drive, stove...), wrongly blocking them and innocent v-e-m style nonsense words. ve stays in the Shifty band for now; a real fix needs a curated exception-word list (have/give/live/love/above/glove/dove...), not a bare grapheme match, since the engine cannot tell short-vowel ve-words from long-vowel magic-e words that end in v. Flagged for the manual tricky/shifty pass, not resolved.
_decisions.soft_g_and_i_ee_restored: 2026-08-06 by Lynden, reviewing 8.4's story words: soft g = /j/ (gorgeous) and unstressed i = /ee/ (glorious) are SHIFTY — a taught letter making one of its other sounds — so both take the slate diamond. 'soft g' sits in promoted_graphemes from 2026-07-03; this restores it to the band for marking purposes, exactly as y=/ee/ and y=/igh/ were restored on 2026-07-26 (PHONICS_PEDAGOGY.md §7) once the diamond became the explanation. allowed_from_level 8 is deliberate: it is the level that needs them now, and anything lower would retro-diamond words in already-approved L6/L7 books.

pronunciations.note: end of a longer word — marked with the slate diamond
end of a one-syllable word — marked with the slate diamond
soft c - before e, i or y (matches the 5.1 Watch Out note, Lynden 2026-07-19)
soft g, before e/i/y (examples must have only one g)

Examples are the diamond-mark word list, not a sample: build_shifty_marks.py turns this column into shifty_marks.json['words'], and a word missing here silently prints a plain digraph dash instead of a diamond. 4.4 shipped with now/down diamonded and how/brown not, on the same page (2026-08-21). Heteronyms (bow, row, sow) are deliberately absent - spelling cannot resolve them, so they need a per-book shifty_marks annotation.
